=== History ===
Saguri Shrine is located in Sayama Saguri and is listed in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}; it is considered to be the "Saguri deity" mentioned in the entry for the 27th day of the 1st month of {{ill|Jōgan|Q1075635|qid=Q1075635|lt=Jōgan}} 1 (859) in the {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|qid=Q1052981|lt=Sandai Jitsuroku}}.

From the medieval period to the Meiji era, because it enshrined a divided spirit of {{ill|Iwashimizu Hachimangū|Q710098|qid=Q710098}}, it was called Atemoto (Ippin) Hachimangū. It appears under that name in the late-Edo gazetteer {{ill|Miyako meisho zue|ja|都名所図会|qid=Q11643495}}, where it is described as "about twenty chō west of Ōkubo, within Sayama village"<ref name="Kumiyama">{{Cite web|url=http://www.town.kumiyama.lg.jp/contents_detail.php?co=cat&frmId=333&frmCd=3-3-1-0-0 |website=Kumiyama Town|title=Saguri Shrine|accessdate=2018-06-02}}</ref>.

=== Precincts ===
=== Honden ===
The scale and style of the honden are three-bay nagare-zukuri (a honden with three front bays), reflecting enshrinement of a divided spirit from Iwashimizu Hachimangū. According to shrine tradition, the honden was likely built around 1494 ({{ill|Meiō|cs|Meió|fa|میئو|ff|Meiō|fr|Ère Meiō|it|Meiō|ja|明応|ko|메이오|ru|Мэйо (нэнго)|simple|Meiō|sr|Меио|sv|Meiō|tr|Meiō|zh|明應 (日本)|qid=Q1193841}} 3), at the end of the {{ill|Muromachi period|Q334845|qid=Q334845}}. The roof is {{ill|cypress bark roof|Q90373477|qid=Q90373477}} (cypress-bark roofing), and has a {{ill|kōhai|Q11415970|qid=Q11415970}} at the front.

Between the bracket complexes of the honden are carved {{ill|kaerumata|Q123117911|qid=Q123117911}} struts: "flowers and birds" on the left and "autumn leaves and deer" on the right. Above the side panels are intricate carvings featuring "squirrels and grapes." In 1980-1981 (Shōwa 55-56), repainting and reroofing were carried out.

=== Camphor tree of Saguri Shrine ===
North of the honden stands a giant {{ill|Camphora officinarum|Q158722|qid=Q158722}}, about 30 m tall with a trunk circumference of 535 cm, estimated at 400-500 years old. A {{ill|Shimenawa|Q1887421|qid=Q1887421}} is wrapped around it, and a small Inari shrine at its base shows that local residents have long revered it as a sacred tree. Because this lowland area was frequently flooded, large trees are relatively rare; together with its vigorous growth, this makes it highly valuable. In June 1993 (Heisei 3), it was selected for "Kyoto's 200 Natural Sites (plant category)," and in February 1994 (Heisei 8) it was designated a town natural monument<ref name="Kumiyama" /><ref name="Kyoto Prefecture">{{Cite web|url=https://www.pref.kyoto.jp/select200/flora44.html |title=Kyoto's 200 Natural Sites: camphor tree of Saguri Shrine |website=Kyoto Prefecture|accessdate=2018-06-02}}</ref>.
